title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Enhancing Superannuation Outcomes For Australians and Helping Australian Businesses Invest) Bill 2021
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Enhancing Superannuation Outcomes For Australians and Helping Australian Businesses Invest) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would broaden access to superannuation contributions and home purchase savings, change contribution and fund tax rules, and extend temporary business asset deductions.
It would remove the $450 monthly earnings threshold for compulsory employer superannuation and lift the First Home Super Saver contribution release limit from $30,000 to $50,000.
Related reforms would retain a work test for deductible personal contributions by older people while supporting separate regulatory changes for other voluntary contributions.
changes: The minimum age for eligible home sale downsizer contributions would fall from 65 to 60.
Eligible people aged 67 to 74 could use the bring-forward arrangements for non-concessional contributions, subject to available cap space.
Superannuation trustees with mixed phases during part of a year could choose how to calculate exempt pension income.
Temporary full expensing of eligible depreciating assets would be extended until 30 June 2023.
summary.affected: Lower-paid employees, employers, first home buyers, older superannuation contributors, fund trustees and eligible businesses would be affected.
